title: HELOC Product Guide
body:
HELOC Product Guide
Owner: Brian Kowalski, Head of Lending
Last updated: 2026-07-30
Audience: Lending, Wealth Management, Compliance, Risk, Operations

Purpose
This guide describes how Halcyon Ridge Capital originates, underwrites, closes, and services Home Equity Lines of Credit (HELOCs). It is the working reference for relationship managers, loan officers, underwriters, and the partner teams who touch a HELOC file. If something here conflicts with the Credit Policy Manual, the Credit Policy Manual wins; please tell me so we can fix this guide.

Product Overview
Our HELOC is a revolving line secured by a first or second lien on a borrower's primary or secondary residence. It is offered mainly to existing Wealth Management clients and to Lending referrals. Key terms:
- Draw period: 10 years, interest-only payments
- Repayment period: 20 years, fully amortizing
- Rate: variable, indexed to Prime plus a margin set by pricing tier
- Maximum combined loan-to-value (CLTV): 80% for primary residences, 70% for second homes
- Line size: $100,000 minimum, $2,500,000 maximum; anything above $1,000,000 needs Head of Lending sign-off
- Minimum credit score: 700 for standard tier, 740 for preferred pricing

Origination Workflow
1. Referral and intake. Relationship Managers in Lending (Brendan Alvarez, Lynn Chase) or Wealth Management (David Montes, Scott Hawkins) open the opportunity in ClientHub and attach the request summary. Loan Officers (Heidi Davis, Cassandra Hampton) own the file from that point.
2. Application. The Loan Officer creates the application in LoanOrigination, which pulls the client profile from ClientHub. Do not re-key client data; if ClientHub is wrong, fix it at the source.
3. KYC/CDD. LoanOrigination depends on KYCPipeline, so no file can advance past application until the client shows a cleared KYC status. Please note that ownership of KYCPipeline moved from Operations to Compliance effective 2026-10-06; questions about screening holds should go to the Compliance KYC specialists (John Smith, Luis Bowen) after that date, and to Operations before it. Sanctions hits are handled by Compliance through SanctionsScreen and are never cleared by Lending.
4. Credit decisioning. Credit Analysts (Jasmine Johnson, Brandi Palmer) run the CreditScoring model, which draws on DataLake, and prepare the credit memo. Senior Underwriters (Joshua Gordon, Tammy Murphy) make the decision within their authority.
5. Collateral. Order an appraisal or automated valuation, a title search, and confirm hazard insurance. Documents are stored in DocVault, which requires AuthSSO access; request access through #it-ops if you cannot open a file.
6. Closing. The Loan Closer (Brandon George) prepares closing documents, confirms the rescission period has expired for primary residences (three business days), and schedules recording of the lien.
7. Funding and setup. Operations releases any initial draw through PaymentsGateway after wire verification, and the accounting entries post to GLCore.

Underwriting Standards
- Maximum debt-to-income ratio of 43% including the proposed line at full utilization
- Documented income and asset verification for all lines above $500,000
- Interest-only draw payments are underwritten at a stressed rate of Prime plus 2.00% to test affordability
- Concentration limits: HELOC exposure in any single metro area is monitored by Credit Risk (Lance Peters, Phillip Jackson, John Garcia) and reviewed monthly
- Exceptions require written approval from the Senior Underwriter and a second sign-off from the Head of Lending; Risk is copied on all exceptions above 5% of monthly volume

Wealth Management Coordination
When a HELOC is being used to fund a securities purchase or a portfolio strategy, the Wealth Advisor must flag it to Lending before application. Portfolio Managers should record the intended use in PortfolioMgr notes. Lines pledged against or alongside a securities-backed facility must be reviewed jointly by Grace Lin's team and Lending to avoid duplicate collateral claims.

Compliance and Monitoring
- Every HELOC file must contain evidence of completed KYC, sanctions screening, and the required disclosures
- Draws are monitored by AMLMonitor; rapid full draws followed by outbound wires are routed to Compliance for review
- Wire requests from a HELOC draw go through WireRoom, which depends on PaymentsGateway and therefore FraudScore. A fraud hold is not overridden by Lending
- Suspicious activity is escalated to Nadia Petrov's AML group; do not discuss a potential SAR with the client

Servicing and Reporting
- Monthly interest statements are generated by the servicing batch and reconciled by Operations; breaks are posted in #recon
- ReportingBI publishes the HELOC portfolio dashboard (balances, utilization, delinquency) using RiskEngine, GLCore, and DataLake feeds. If numbers look stale, check #it-ops before escalating
- Delinquency over 30 days triggers a handoff to the Lending servicing queue and a notice to the relationship owner

Common Pitfalls
- Starting a file before KYC clears causes rework and aged pipeline
- Missing flood zone determinations delay closing
- Skipping the rescission calendar check leads to premature funding

Contacts
Product questions: Brian Kowalski. Underwriting: Joshua Gordon or Tammy Murphy. Closing: Brandon George. Compliance: Marcus Bell's team via #compliance. System issues: #it-ops, or #incidents for outages. Suggested edits to this guide are welcome at any time.
